explanation: Compared against OEIS A237413: a(n) counts ways to write n = k + m (k, m > 0) with p(k)²−2, p(m)²−2 and p(p(m))²−2 all prime, where p(j) is the j-th prime; conjecture a(n) > 0 for n > 1. In `a`, k ranges over [1, n), m = n − k ≥ 1, p(j) = Nat.nth Nat.Prime (j−1), and p(p(m)) = nth (nth (m−1) − 1), all correctly 1-indexed. The values a(1..5) = 0,1,2,2,2 match the data. Faithful.
